newsitem.title: INDIA: India approves $180 million in foreign investments.
newsitem.headline: India approves $180 million in foreign investments.

text.p: India on Wednesday cleared 6.5 billion rupees ($180 million) worth of investments by foreign firms including units of U.S. giants IBM, General Electric Co and Mobil Corp.
The Industry Ministry said in a statement that the Foreign Investment Promotion Board approved 58 investment proposals for products ranging from syringes to yeast.

India began opening its doors to foreign investment in 1991 as part of an economic liberalisation programme, but has attracted relatively small amounts of foreign direct investment compared to neighbouring China.

In 1994, India attracted $620 million in foreign direct investment, well below China's $43 billion, according to the World Bank. In the fiscal year that ended on March 31, foreign firms pumped $2.0 billion in direct investments into India.
The Indian government has set a goal of attracting $10 billion a year in foreign direct investment -- but has fixed no time frame.

The board, which is headed by the Industry Ministry and responsible for all but the largest and most controversial foreign investment proposals, approved a 1.05-billion-rupee investment by U.S.-based Becton Dickinson and Co.
Becton Dickinson's investment, the largest on the list, would finance the creation of a wholly-owned subsidiary to make needle syringes.
The board cleared a 720-million-rupee investment by a unit of International Business Machines Corp (IBM) in an 80-percent owned computer software subsidiary.
IBM World Trade Corp will set up the computer software unit in the southern city of Bangalore, it said.

New Delhi approved a 350-million-rupee investment by a unit of General Electric Co (GE) in a lighting components subsidiary. It said GE Lighting (India) Ltd would set up the wholly-owned subsidiary in Bombay.
Warner-Lambert India Pvt Ltd, a unit of U.S.-based Warner-Lambert Co, will invest 315 million rupees in a wholly-owned pharmaceutical unit.
Mobil Asia Pacific Pte Ltd won clearance to invest 175 million rupees in a wholly-owned petroleum products subsidiary. It gave no other details.
The board approved a proposal by BZW Worldwide Holdings Ltd to invest 175 million rupees in a 75-percent owned financial services unit.
Fiat Engineering Spa, a unit of Italy's Fiat Spa, was granted permission to set up a wholly-owned engineering and consultancy subsidiary with an investment of 35 million rupees.
The board allowed a 27.7-million-rupee investment by Baxter India Pvt Ltd, a unit of Baxter International Inc of the United States, in a wholly-owned medical products subsidiary.

It cleared a proposal by Citicorp Information Technology Industries Ltd, a unit of U.S.-based Citicorp, to pay 15.8 million rupees for a 41.8 percent stake in a financial services unit. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
